$comment: Which screen reaches each API route, checked by web/scripts/check-screen-coverage.mjs.
The route list is derived from api/src/**/*.controller.ts and is not edited here:
a route this file does not mention fails the build, and an entry naming no route
fails it too. Adding an endpoint means adding a line here in the same commit.
Exactly one of `screen`, `waived_to` or `no_screen_owed` per entry. A `screen` is a
repository-relative path and must exist; anything more a reader needs goes in `note`.
A `waived_to` must name one of the `stages` declared above -- without that the naming
requirement is satisfied by any non-empty string. `no_screen_owed` is for a route no
person ever reaches. The latter two carry a reason, because nothing can check either.
Thirteen of the thirty-five are reached by a screen today; twenty-one are waived and
one owes none. That is the interface debt Stage 3 and Stage 4 accumulated with
nothing recording it (ruling of 2026-09-06), written down rather than discovered at
the pilot. The check prints these three numbers, so they are read rather than trusted.

routes.note: Called from every authenticated screen rather than from one.

routes.reason: §8 asks for the chain when a profile is opened, and the profile screen does not request it yet. My Network is where it lands.
Reassignment is the highest-risk authorization surface in the system (§5). My Network is the screen that performs it.
Admin-only (§7, people.correct_sex), and it forces a Network change. It belongs to the Admin surface §19 describes, which the pilot does not need.
Account provisioning is Admin's operational responsibility (§6, §19). The pilot's accounts are provisioned before it starts.
Resending an activation email is Admin operations, alongside provisioning above.
The Cell roster (§12). Cell Attendance reads it, and it is the roster view §12 keeps separate from the statistical report.
Adding a member is part of running a Cell during the pilot month (§10).
The other half of membership, and a move is one transaction (§10).
A schedule change decides which meetings a month derives, so a pilot month needs it reachable (§10, §13).
Cell Meetings. §19 puts meetings awaiting a record above the numbers on every leader's dashboard.
Who there is to record (§13). Cell Meetings calls it before a submission.
Recording a meeting is the thing the pilot exists to test — whether leaders record every week.
The DCC checklist (§9). A leader marking it must see who is already marked.
DCC recording, the second half of the pilot's month cycle (§9).
Direct creation is Admin's during the initial-encoding phase (§2, §10). The pilot's Cells exist before it starts.
Configuration rather than operation (§10). Nothing in one pilot month requires changing a category.
A closure is never reversed (decision 0133), so it is deliberately not put in front of a pilot leader.
Request-and-approve is how a Cell is created or changes hands (§10). One branch running one month needs neither.
The Admin queue §19 describes. It pairs with the approve and decline routes below.
The Admin queue's action (§10). A pending request changes nothing until it is decided.
The other outcome of the queue, and a decision is final (decision 0147).
The liveness probe (§24). It is called by the deployment platform and never by a person, so no stage will ever owe it a screen.
